results.corrected_claim: The finding is correct. Apple's DocC metadata.platforms for Glass (`struct Glass`), View.glassEffect(_:in:) (`nonisolated func glassEffect(_ glass: Glass = .regular, in shape: some Shape = DefaultGlassEffectShape()) -> some View`) and GlassEffectContainer (`@MainActor @preconcurrency struct GlassEffectContainer<Content> where Content : View`) lists only iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS and watchOS, all introducedAt 26.0 with beta and deprecated false. visionOS is not listed. The same platform set, also without visionOS, appears on View.glassEffectTransition(_:), GlassEffectTransition, Glass.identity and PrimitiveButtonStyle.glass. Other 26.0 SwiftUI symbols do list visionOS 26.0: ConcentricRectangle, DefaultToolbarItem, DefaultToolbarItem.init(kind:placement:), View.tabBarMinimizeBehavior(_:), Edge.Corner.Style, Shape.rect(corners:isUniform:) and View.containerShape(_:). So the omission is deliberate, not a docs gap. The skill wrongly claims visionOS 26 in four places: 01-api-reference.md §15 line 532 ('visionOS | 26.0+'), SKILL.md line 3 (description), SKILL.md line 5 (platforms key) and README.md line 90. The §15 table also leaves out Mac Catalyst 26.0+, which Apple lists. visionOS has its own, different glass API: `nonisolated func glassBackgroundEffect(displayMode: GlassBackgroundDisplayMode = .always) -> some View`, which is visionOS 1.0+ only. HIG Materials says, verbatim: 'In visionOS, windows generally use an unmodifiable system-defined material called glass that helps people stay grounded...'. The September 2026 and June 2026 sections of the SwiftUI updates page contain nothing about glass or visionOS, so nothing changed for iOS 27.
results.notes: Sources are all apple-doc JSON: glass.json, view/glasseffect(_:in:).json, glasseffectcontainer.json, primitivebuttonstyle/glass.json, view/glassbackgroundeffect(displaymode:).json, concentricrectangle.json, defaulttoolbaritem.json, view/tabbarminimizebehavior(_:).json and updates/swiftui.json (September/June 2026 sections). The HIG quote is from design/human-interface-guidelines/materials.json (apple-other). I checked the skill text with grep: 01 line 532, SKILL.md lines 3 and 5, README line 90, and the 01 table at lines 526-534, which has no Mac Catalyst row. The docs appear to be the current Xcode 27 build: declarations carry newer attributes such as @export(implementation) and @ContentBuilder. Even so, glassEffect, Glass and GlassEffectContainer still have no visionOS entry. A suggested fix is to drop visionOS from the Liquid Glass target lists and add Mac Catalyst 26.0+. If visionOS stays as an activation trigger, the skill should say to use glassBackgroundEffect there, not glassEffect.

results.corrected_claim: The finding is correct. The shipping declaration is `nonisolated func glassEffect(_ glass: Glass = .regular, in shape: some Shape = DefaultGlassEffectShape()) -> some View`, with no isEnabled parameter. The string 'isEnabled' appears nowhere in the glassEffect(_:in:) JSON. The only glassEffect-family references are glassEffect(_:in:), glassEffectID(_:in:), glassEffectTransition(_:) and glassEffectUnion(id:namespace:). The guessed path view/glasseffect(_:in:isenabled:).json returns 404. The transition modifier is `@MainActor @preconcurrency func glassEffectTransition(_ transition: GlassEffectTransition) -> some View`, also with no isEnabled, and 'isEnabled' appears nowhere on that page. Glass.identity is `static var identity: Glass { get }`, abstract: 'The identity variant of glass. When applied, your content remains unaffected as if no glass effect was applied.' So conditional glass should be written as `.glassEffect(flag ? .regular : .identity, in: shape)`. I confirmed every skill location: 01 lines 7, 19, 29 and 51; 01 §6 lines 224 and 231; 02 lines 133 and 166; 06 lines 63 and 162; 07 lines 124 (prose) and 127. No file in examples/*.swift uses isEnabled.
results.notes: Sources are apple-doc JSON: view/glasseffect(_:in:).json, view/glasseffecttransition(_:).json, glass/identity.json and glasseffecttransition.json, plus a 404 on the guessed isEnabled overload path. The WWDC25 session 323 page (apple-video) has no isEnabled usage either. The June/September 2026 SwiftUI updates add no glass APIs. One related error is outside this finding: 01 line 234 declares `enum GlassEffectTransition`, but Apple declares it as `struct GlassEffectTransition`. Its type properties are identity ('The identity transition specifying no changes.'), matchedGeometry and materialize. The skill text also calls .materialize a gradual light modulation; it was not checked in depth. Also outside this finding: 01 line 14 shows a separate `func glassEffect()` overload and line 18 shows the default `DefaultGlassEffectShape` without parentheses. In reality, glassEffect() is just glassEffect(_:in:) called with its defaults, and the default value is `DefaultGlassEffectShape()`.

results.corrected_claim: The finding is correct, with one precision fix. The real declaration is `static func concentric(minimum: Edge.Corner.Style? = nil) -> Edge.Corner.Style`. The declaration tokens include the `= nil` default, which the metadata fragments leave out. Edge.Corner.Style (`struct Style`, 26.0 on all seven platforms including visionOS, ExpressibleByFloatLiteral and ExpressibleByIntegerLiteral) has exactly these members: `static var concentric`, `concentric(minimum:)` and `fixed(_:)`. The shape API is `static func rect(corners: Edge.Corner.Style, isUniform: Bool = false) -> Self`; the docs prefix it with `@export(implementation)`. ConcentricRectangle (`struct ConcentricRectangle`) is iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS 26.0+. The skill's form cannot compile. Its label `cornerRadius:` resolves to `static func rect(cornerRadius: CGFloat, style: RoundedCornerStyle = .continuous) -> Self` ('Available when Self is RoundedRectangle'), and CGFloat has no `.containerConcentric` member. 'containerConcentric' appears nowhere on the ConcentricRectangle or Edge.Corner.Style pages. The parent shape comes from `nonisolated func containerShape(_ shape: some RoundedRectangularShape) -> some View` (26.0, all platforms including visionOS). Its abstract, verbatim: 'Sets the container shape to use for any container relative shape or concentric rectangle within this view.' The correct replacement is `.glassEffect(.regular, in: .rect(corners: .concentric, isUniform: true))` or `ConcentricRectangle()`. Optionally use `.concentric(minimum: 12)`. Inside a custom rounded parent, also add `.containerShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 28))` on that parent. I confirmed every location: SKILL.md line 87; 01 §12 lines 466 and 473-475; 02 lines 20, 27, 82 and 154; 03 lines 13, 18 and 152; 07 §6 line 154; checklist line 26; glass-card-stack.md line 92. No file in examples/*.swift uses it.
results.notes: Sources are apple-doc JSON: concentricrectangle.json, edge/corner/style.json, edge/corner/style/concentric(minimum:).json (raw declaration tokens checked), shape/rect(corners:isuniform:).json, shape/rect(cornerradius:style:).json and view/containershape(_:)-3br47.json. This also explains where the name came from. WWDC25 session 323 (apple-video) showed a pre-release snippet, `.background(.tint, in: .rect(corner: .containerConcentric))`, with the narration 'Pass the containerConcentric configuration to the corner parameter of a rectangle'. On Apple Developer Forums thread 787615 (apple-other, June 2025), a Frameworks Engineer answered 'These APIs aren't available in the first beta release.' The API shipped as `.rect(corners: .concentric, isUniform:)` and ConcentricRectangle. The skill's `cornerRadius:` label never matched even the WWDC spelling. ConcentricRectangle's overview says concentric corners can compute to 0 (square) when far from the container corner, and recommends `concentric(minimum:)` in that case.

results.corrected_claim: The finding is correct. DefaultToolbarItem is `nonisolated struct DefaultToolbarItem` (iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS 26.0+). Its relationships section lists exactly one conformance, ToolbarContent; View is not among them. Its abstract, verbatim: 'A toolbar item that represents a system component.' The finding's init signature leaves out a default. The exact initializer is `nonisolated init(kind: ToolbarDefaultItemKind, placement: ToolbarItemPlacement = .automatic)`. ToolbarItem is `nonisolated struct ToolbarItem<ID, Content> where Content : View`, and its `nonisolated init(placement: ToolbarItemPlacement = .automatic, @ContentBuilder content: () -> Content)` requires 'Content conforms to View'. A DefaultToolbarItem therefore cannot be the content of a ToolbarItem, and the nested form in the skill fails to type-check. This holds even with Xcode 27's ContentBuilder. Apple's own init(kind:placement:) example places `DefaultToolbarItem(kind: .search, placement: .bottomBar)` directly in `.toolbar { }`, next to ToolbarItem and ToolbarSpacer entries. Fix both copies: 01 §10 lines 420-424 and patterns/glass-search-field.md lines 58-62.
results.notes: Sources are apple-doc JSON: defaulttoolbaritem.json, defaulttoolbaritem/init(kind:placement:).json, toolbaritem.json and toolbaritem/init(placement:content:).json. WWDC25 session 323 (apple-video), in its 'Toolbar items with flexible spacing' snippet, also places DefaultToolbarItem(kind: .search, placement: .bottomBar) directly in the .toolbar builder between ToolbarSpacer items. The init(kind:placement:) discussion adds that 'Combinations of kind and placement may be valid on some platforms, but not on others'. It also says that placing a DefaultToolbarItem with .search in a NavigationSplitView column picks the column that shows search in compact width, but only when the search modifier is on the NavigationSplitView. The June 2026 updates make ContentBuilder 'the unified replacement for type-specific builders like ToolbarContentBuilder'. ToolbarItem's content closure is now @ContentBuilder but is still constrained to View.

results.corrected_claim:
The finding is correct. 02-hig-principles.md leaves out every one of these HIG Materials points, all verified verbatim:
- 'Only use clear Liquid Glass for components that appear over visually rich backgrounds.'
- 'Use the regular variant when background content might create legibility issues, or when components have a significant amount of text, such as alerts, sidebars, or popovers.'
- 'If the underlying content is bright, consider adding a dark dimming layer of 35% opacity.'
- 'If the underlying content is sufficiently dark, or if you use standard media playback controls from AVKit that provide their own dimming layer, you don't need to apply a dimming layer.'
- 'An exception to this is for controls in the content layer with a transient interactive element like sliders and toggles; in these cases, the element takes on a Liquid Glass appearance to emphasize its interactivity when a person activates it.'
- 'Use Liquid Glass effects sparingly.'
- 'The appearance of these variants can differ in response to certain system settings, like if people choose a preferred look for Liquid Glass in their device's settings, or turn on accessibility settings that reduce transparency or increase contrast in the interface.'

The newest change-log entry is 'September 9, 2025 | Updated guidance for Liquid Glass.' There is no 2026 entry. HIG Materials sets no limit on how many layers can be stacked. The skill's 'Maximum two glass layers stacked' rule (02 lines 65 and 160, SKILL.md line 85, checklist line 21) has no source. It also contradicts WWDC25 session 219, which the skill itself cites: 'always avoid glass on glass Stacking Liquid Glass elements on top of each other can quickly make the interface feel cluttered and confusing.' and 'When placing elements on top of Liquid Glass, avoid applying the material to both layers. Instead, use fills, transparency, and vibrancy for the top elements...'. So the skill's line 'A glass card sitting on a glass nav bar = OK' is wrong.
results.notes: Sources are the HIG materials.json (apple-other) and the WWDC25 session 219 transcript at developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/219/ (apple-video). Session 219 also says 'Clear should only be used when these 3 conditions are met' and describes localized dimming. I read the HIG text through a summarizing fetch tool, so I re-checked the key sentences in a second, targeted fetch: 35%, sparingly, preferred look, sliders and toggles, the change-log top row, and the absence of any layer-count rule. The gap is specific to the 02 distillation; other skill files cover part of it. 01 line 81 and 03 line 93 recommend .clear over photos and video. 01 line 497 and 05 lines 17 and 163 mention 'Tinted Mode (iOS 26.1+)', which is the user-selectable look. No skill file has the 35% dimming guidance, the 'regular for text-heavy components' rule, the sliders/toggles exception, or 'Use Liquid Glass effects sparingly'; 02 and SKILL.md only say 'Tint sparingly'.
